decisions.decision: Extended-ID flag ESTABLISHED with confidence: `StatusBitField & ics.SPY_STATUS_XTD_FRAME` (0x4), not `ics.SPY_STATUS_EXTENDED` (0x80000000).
decisions.rationale: SPY_STATUS_XTD_FRAME sits in the coherent low-order per-frame flag family (SPY_STATUS_GLOBAL_ERR=0x1, TX_MSG=0x2, XTD_FRAME=0x4, REMOTE_FRAME=0x8, CRC_ERROR=0x10 -- sequential single-bit flags describing one specific frame). SPY_STATUS_EXTENDED sits in a separate high-bit tier (0x20000000/0x40000000/0x80000000) alongside SPY_STATUS_CANFD/HIGH_SPEED/INIT_MESSAGE -- device/mode-level flags, not per-frame identity -- and SPY_STATUS_CANFD and SPY_STATUS_INIT_MESSAGE both equal 0x20000000 (overloaded/context-dependent), which rules that tier out as a reliable simple per-frame flag space. Corroborated by symmetry with src/new_logger.py's existing working TX code, which already sets `msg.StatusBitField = ics.SPY_STATUS_XTD_FRAME` to mark an outgoing frame extended on the exact same field of the exact same SpyMessage type sent to the exact same hardware -- same field, same bit, set on TX and expected back on RX. Verified live via `ics.SPY_STATUS_XTD_FRAME` etc. in this session (see context_notes for the exact values captured).

decisions.decision: Timestamp unit/epoch NOT established with confidence -- must be implemented behind a named constant explicitly labelled UNCONFIRMED in both code and the eventual SUMMARY, and routed to the hardware bring-up check per the plan's own instruction. Do NOT resolve this by guessing.
decisions.rationale: Two genuinely conflicting/incomplete signals found this session, neither resolvable without real hardware: (1) `SpyMessage.TimeSystem`'s own docstring (captured live via help(ics.SpyMessage)) reads verbatim 'TimeSystem is loaded with the value received from the timeGetTime call in the WIN32 multimedia API' -- i.e. milliseconds, from a Windows-specific API, with an arbitrary system-uptime-relative epoch that wraps roughly every 49.7 days as a DWORD. The actual deployment target is Linux (CM4), so this Windows-specific docstring text may not even describe what the same attribute name reports on the real hardware -- the compiled extension could report something entirely different there. (2) src/new_logger.py's existing (unverified) legacy code formats `m.TimeSystem` with `f'{ts:.6f}'` under a CSV header of 'timestamp_s', implying an assumption that the raw value is already fractional seconds -- which directly contradicts the vendor docstring's 'milliseconds from timeGetTime' description (though it is NOT actually a contradiction in the strictest sense: an integer millisecond count formatted with 6 decimal places just displays trailing zeros and LOOKS like seconds.microseconds without being wrong data -- this is itself an ambiguity, not a resolved fact). (3) A second candidate API exists, `ics.get_timestamp_for_msg(device, msg)`, whose own docstring/example (captured live) returns a bare `Float` with no unit or epoch documented at all (example output 354577568.9145524 -- plausible as seconds since an arbitrary/hardware-relative epoch given the magnitude, but this is inference, not a vendor statement). RESEARCH.md's own Assumption A2 already flagged this exact area ('python-ics's hardware timestamp (m.TimeSystem) ... not directly compared for accuracy/resolution this session') as untested. This is precisely the kind of fact the plan says must be carried forward as a labelled assumption, not promoted to fact.

decisions.decision: Exception-type landmine found and must be respected in Task 2 (and reused in Task 1's device-open path): `ics.RuntimeError` is NOT a subclass of the Python builtin `RuntimeError`.
decisions.rationale: Verified live this session: `issubclass(ics.RuntimeError, RuntimeError)` returns `False`; `ics.RuntimeError.__mro__` is `(ics.ics.RuntimeError, Exception, BaseException, object)` -- it inherits directly from `Exception`, bypassing the builtin `RuntimeError` entirely. Confirmed this is the actual exception type raised by real calls in this environment: `ics.find_devices()` with no driver present raised `<class 'ics.ics.RuntimeError'>` (message: "Error: find_devices(): Failed to Retrieve address of function 'icsneoFindDevices': Windows Error #127 for library 'icsneo40.dll'"). The plan's Task 2 behavior block requires 'an exception raised by the SDK's message-poll call is caught by its own type' -- a bare `except RuntimeError:` would silently NOT catch this and let it propagate uncaught, which is exactly the failure mode CAP-06 exists to prevent. The implementation must catch the exception type off the injected SDK object itself (e.g. `sdk.RuntimeError`), never the builtin, so the fake SDK used in tests and the real `ics` module both work identically through the same seam.
